# Collage and composition

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Frames built from pieces: cut-outs, collage, mirrored layouts, negative space and one huge subject. 13 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Hard split: image half, text half

`dv-hard-split-screen` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · any

The frame divides vertically: one half a mockup or picture, the other half a ground with type; the image half can carry a stepped dithered border.

- **Build:** Recipe: two full-frame backdrop plane halves with their own content. Anatomy: 50/50 split; cuts swap both halves together. Sound: Cuts on beats.
- **Timing:** About 95 f per pair.
- **Use when:** Product plus claim, side by side.
- **Avoid when:** Centred copy in the text half (left-align it).

### One composition rule per act

`dv-act-composition-rule` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy calm · any

An act keeps exactly one centred object on black for its whole length (a dot, a line, a triangle, a prism), then the next act flips to an off-centre cropped stage: the composition change marks the act change.

- **Build:** Recipe: a layout rule per act in the timeline. Anatomy: Centred single object vs off-centre crop. Sound: A section change on the switch.
- **Timing:** Acts of 2-3 s.
- **Use when:** Films with a construction act and a product act.
- **Avoid when:** Mixing the two rules within one act.

### One huge centred subject

`lc-one-centred-subject` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy any · any

Every frame has exactly one subject, centred and large: a single line of type, or one 3D slab scaled to most of the frame width and often bleeding past the edges, with everything else dimmed.

- **Build:** Compose every shot on the frame centre (on safeBox cy in a tall frame) with exactly one subject: a single line of type sized with fitSize to at most 80% of the frame width, or one 3D slab scaled through the anchor camera to at least 0.85 of the frame width and bleeding past the edges wherever its content allows, so it reads as the product filling the frame rather than a centred floating card. Show captured stage at about 2x native, so body text is at least 27 px at 1080p. Dim anything that is not the hero to brightness 0.6-0.7, or defocus it with RackFocus (blur 8-40); never leave it at full strength. Keep each hold alive with breath(t, 0.025) on the camera.
- **Timing:** Holds of 30-72 f per hero. Cards at 85-100% of frame width or bleeding past it, header bars up to full width, tables at least 80%; type 5-8% of frame height per line. Dims and rack focus 12-20 f on E.smooth.
- **Use when:** Fast, phone-first films; walkthroughs where the viewer must never search for the subject; the default framing between more designed compositions.
- **Avoid when:** Comparison or cause-and-effect beats that need two things on screen at once (use a split), or bento-style loops.

### Subtract to the one

`lc-subtract-to-one` · layout and composition · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A busy board loses its elements one by one until a single survivor remains, which either re-centres or stays exactly where it was while the world around it dims.

- **Build:** Staccato version: keep an array of tiles and an index that drops by one at keyframes 5-7 f apart, decided with fd(). Recompute the centred flex layout for each state with no tween, so the survivors jump to their new centred positions on each removal, and hold the last one for 17 f with a +0.5% scale drift. Graded version: duplicate the survivor into a top layer at identical coordinates, fade every neighbour over 12 f on E.smooth, then darken the stage plate from C.paper to C.ink with mixColor over 10 f on E.in, leaving the survivor crisp in place. Words in a line leave in reading order, each lifting 12 px and fading over 4 f on E.in, 3 f apart; if the survivor must end centred, slide it home with spr(f, s, SPR.soft) once the others are gone.
- **Timing:** Staccato: a removal every 5-7 f; last survivor held 17 f. Graded: neighbours fade over 12 f, world dims over 10 f, hold 30 f. Word exits 4 f each, 3 f apart (a line clears in about 12 f). Re-centre 20-40 f on SPR.soft.
- **Use when:** Isolating the deliverable, the found result or the keyword before entering its world; turning a crowded problem state into one focus.
- **Avoid when:** The removed elements are themselves the message (show them first), or the survivor is small enough to float lost in an empty frame (push in after isolating it).

### A set of physical objects as the film's vocabulary

`dv-object-vocabulary` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Logos become die-cut stickers with a white border and a soft shadow lying on a cutting mat; letters sit on square tiles that drift apart radially under a pull-back, each at its own speed.

- **Build:** Cutouts with paper border; tiles as Cards with radial drift. Anatomy: Sticker border 6-8 px, contact shadow; tiles about 70 px each with one letter. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** Static, or a radial drift over 36 f.
- **Use when:** Tabletop, crafted films.
- **Avoid when:** Mixing object styles.

### Cards flick onto a pile

`dv-card-pile-on` · layout and composition · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

New photo cards pop onto the top of a fanned stack one after another, each starting small and motion-blurred, the cadence decaying until the cut; inside a framed screen, cards spin in toward level, pile up and orbit as a ring.

- **Build:** Cards cardArrive (rot, scale from 0.7) with starts on a decaying list. Anatomy: Arrival 6 f each; one card every 9-10 f, decaying; spin 10 f; orbit 100 f in two pushes. Sound: A beat bed; a wood-block hit. Materials: A new card is born inside the face of the current top card: small (35 % of a card) and heavily blurred (20 px for 2-4 f) over its right half, it grows and turns toward the viewer (yaw 15 -> 5 deg in perspective) and lands as the new top card with a soft drop shadow appearing; about 12 f per card, one every 24 f.
- **Materials:** A new card is born inside the face of the current top card: small (35 % of a card) and heavily blurred (20 px for 2-4 f) over its right half, it grows and turns toward the viewer (yaw 15 -> 5 deg in perspective) and lands as the new top card with a soft drop shadow appearing; about 12 f per card, one every 24 f.
- **Timing:** 60-110 f.
- **Use when:** Accumulation: saves, uploads, picks.
- **Avoid when:** Even cadence.

### Centre object with mirrored flanks

`lc-symmetric-flank` · layout and composition · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A narrow centre object (a phone-width window, a pill, a big number) holds the middle while matching elements sit on both sides: the two halves of a caption, or two mirrored columns of items.

- **Build:** Build a three-column row centred on (W/2, H/2): [left flank, right-aligned] [centre object] [right flank, left-aligned], with a 3% W gutter (58 px at 1080p) between each flank and the object. Caption version: split the sentence so the object stands in for a word, and reveal the halves with Words (blur to focus), the right half 20-42 f after the left. Column version: two columns of 80 px items, rows offset alternately by half a row, the right column built as the mirror of the left. Rows appear top to bottom in sync on both sides, 6 f per row (opacity plus a 10 px rise, 12 f on E.out); then both columns drift outward with a U-shaped speed while the centre statement rises 50 px over 38 f on E.outSoft.
- **Timing:** Caption halves 20-42 f apart; hold about 60 f. Column rows 6 f apart (five rows in about 30 f); outward drift 3.8, then 0.7, then 1.8 px/f over about 120 f. Centre numeral rises 50 px over 38 f.
- **Use when:** A narrow device or pill leaves empty sides; a stat that needs visible volume on either side; inputs and outputs around one product; the tagline that frames a logo pill before the end.
- **Avoid when:** Wide centre subjects (each flank gets squeezed under 20% of the frame), or vertical formats (stack above and below instead).

### Hub-and-spoke concept diagram

`lc-hub-spoke-diagram` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A central product tile sits inside two thin concentric rings with a short streak orbiting it, inputs on the left and outputs on the right, under a centred one-line headline.

- **Build:** Centre an opaque 64-96 px icon tile with a soft shadow, and draw two SVG circles around it at 1.8x and 2.8x the tile size: 1.5 px strokes at 15% opacity. The orbiting streak is an SVG arc of about 70 deg on the outer ring, with stroke opacity ramping from 0 to 1 toward its head (a one-hue linearGradient in C.accent), turned by rotate(1.5 * f deg). Inputs (left) and outputs (right) are small opaque labelled chips in mirrored rows that enter together, 6 f per row (opacity plus a 10 px rise, 12 f on E.out); then connector lines from each chip to the outer ring draw with stroke-dashoffset over 16 f on E.out. The headline above reveals with Words, and the orbit keeps the hold alive.
- **Timing:** Rows 6 f apart, 12 f each; connectors 16 f on E.out; streak 1.5 deg/f (a quarter turn per second) on E.linear. Hold 120-200 f; the rotation keeps it moving.
- **Use when:** Explaining a many-inputs, many-outputs product (integrations, sources to results) in one still composition without narration; the concept beat before a walkthrough.
- **Avoid when:** More than five chips per side, or when the real 3D subject can show the same thing directly.

### Objects pop around a word at full size

`dv-pop-around-word` · layout and composition · accent · energy high · launch, feature

Around a word or a stacked lockup, sticker objects, ad images or tilted 3D badges pop on at full size, no scale or fade, staggered by 1-4 frames (one settles 7 px), framing the word with context.

- **Build:** HardStep visibility per object, positions laid around the word's box. Anatomy: Cut-ons at full size; tilts 5-15 deg; lines 2-3 f apart. Sound: Chat pops. Materials: The chips pop exactly where the next words land, so for about 20 f the sentence is tangled with the logos (text over chips, no knockout; chips tilted -25 to +20 deg, white pills with a 1 px border at 6 % and a 6 % shadow); then the chips drift about 220 px upward on an expo-out and the line clears (cleared by 0.7 s).
- **Materials:** The chips pop exactly where the next words land, so for about 20 f the sentence is tangled with the logos (text over chips, no knockout; chips tilted -25 to +20 deg, white pills with a 1 px border at 6 % and a 6 % shadow); then the chips drift about 220 px upward on an expo-out and the line clears (cleared by 0.7 s).
- **Timing:** 1 f each; 1-4 f stagger.
- **Use when:** Showing what a word covers (integrations, formats, uses).
- **Avoid when:** More than about eight objects.

### Tiles in a mixed shape vocabulary

`dv-shape-vocabulary` · layout and composition · accent · energy calm · any

A layout uses a small set of shapes (circles, a rounded square, pills, photos with asymmetric corners), flat colour blocks mixed among photos, tinted photo cards, coloured tag chips and side accent bars, all cropped by the frame.

- **Build:** Recipe: per-tile corner radius arrays; colour blocks as Cards. Anatomy: Mixed radii (one corner fully round, others small); colour blocks 40-120 px. Sound: Pops and a ding. Materials: Every frame device is drawn from the logo's parts before the logo appears: the photo mask, the hairline caption frames, the pair of circles and the blobs are the mark's rounded rect, its circular cut-out and its dot; a construction drawing shows the primitives with anchor nodes; the film resolves on their assembly.
- **Materials:** Every frame device is drawn from the logo's parts before the logo appears: the photo mask, the hairline caption frames, the pair of circles and the blobs are the mark's rounded rect, its circular cut-out and its dot; a construction drawing shows the primitives with anchor nodes; the film resolves on their assembly.
- **Timing:** Static after the unfold; tags pop 4-8 f.
- **Use when:** Bento and collage layouts that should feel designed, not templated.
- **Avoid when:** Every tile the same radius.

### Arc carousel

`lc-arc-carousel` · layout and composition · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

A row of cards rides a wide smile-shaped arc across the lower part of the frame, each tilted tangent to the curve, rushing in, coasting slowly through the middle and speeding out.

- **Build:** Use a circle of R = 1750 px centred at (960, -790) at 1080p. Card i sits at angle theta_i = theta0(f) + i * 11 deg, with x = 960 + R sin(theta_i), y = -790 + R cos(theta_i) and rotateZ(-theta_i), so the arc bottoms out at y = 960 and the cards lean outward toward the edges. Drive it with a U-shaped speed: theta0(f) = 12 deg * (1 - prog(f, 0, 45, E.out)) - 0.25 deg * (f - 45) - 7.6 deg * prog(f, 45, 90, E.in), over 12 opaque cards with soft drop shadows, z-ordered so the centre card is on top. Behind them, a large flat ellipse (or one accent hue fading to transparent) centred above the arc acts as the dome. Apply the motion-blur pass while card speed exceeds 12 px/f (roughly the first 15 f and the last 20 f).
- **Timing:** 90 f per pass. Card speed 58 px/f on entry, about 8 px/f through the middle, 39 px/f on exit (angular 1.9, then 0.25, then 1.3 deg/f). Spacing 11 deg, about 336 px of arc, for cards 260-300 px wide.
- **Use when:** Showing an inventory or collection (templates, cards, products, integrations) where several items should read at once and the set should feel endless; a looping feature beat.
- **Avoid when:** Items with dense text that must be read at the edges (tilted edge cards are glanced at, not read), or vertical frames where the arc gets too tight.

### Four de-synchronised mini-films in a gutterless grid

`dv-quad-grid-films` · layout and composition · signature · energy high · loop, launch, feature

The frame is split into four panels with no gutters (or near-invisible hairlines), each running its own mini-film in its own style; cuts happen in one panel at a time on an irregular clock (never two on the same frame, at least two panels always moving); motifs echo across panels; near the loop's end the panels relay scenes to each other so the loop never visibly restarts.

- **Build:** Recipe: orthographic 2D grid 2x2, each cell a scaled 1920x1080 composition in looping sub-scene with awkward periods; merge all cut frames and nudge apart any within 6 f. Anatomy: Panels 960 x 540 at 1080p; per-panel state changes about every 1 s; cut gaps 12-88 f at 60 fps, irregular; a motif from one panel reappearing (inverted) in another. Sound: One shared bed; pane cuts driven by SFX onsets (whooshes, pops, keypresses), not the beat.
- **Timing:** Panel cuts 12-88 f apart; relays 16 f apart at the loop end.
- **Use when:** Social loops and hero loops that must show breadth; feature reels.
- **Avoid when:** Synchronised cuts across panels; 9:16 frames (panels get too small).

### Swarm, cluster and burst reveal

`lc-swarm-cluster-burst` · layout and composition · signature · energy high · launch, sting

About twenty cards or screenshots fly in from every edge, swirl, pack into a dense overlapping cluster that slowly swells, then blow outward past the camera to uncover a hero object that was waiting behind them.

- **Build:** Place the hero (lockup, stat card, product) centred at z 0, already at final size, with N = 16-24 cards above it. Give card i a slot in a packed cluster (a grid jittered by rand(i): up to 40 px and 6 deg, overlapping, larger cards higher in z) and a unit radial vector from the centre through that slot. Fly-in: set the card's offset along its vector to total - inertia(f, s_i, 56, 0.95).x, so it starts about 1090 px out and coasts into its slot, with start frames spread by stagger(i, N, 24, E.out). Over the next 60 f the slots rotate about the centre by an angle that decays from 24 deg to 0 on E.outSoft (the swirl), contract to 73% spread over 32 f on E.out, and then the whole cluster scales up linearly by 0.2% per frame. Burst: each card travels along its vector by d(n) = 3n^2 px for n <= 12, then 432 + 72(n - 12), with scale 1 + 2(n/24)^3 under a true motion-blur pass, so the hero is uncovered in about 18 f.
- **Timing:** Fly-in 28-40 f, entering at 56 px/f and decaying. Swirl 60 f. Converge 32 f (cluster width 1474 to 1076 px at 1080p). Build 104 f at +0.2%/f, E.linear. Burst 24 f, peaking at 72 px/f with motion blur; the last cards clear by f24, then hold the hero. Shorter scatter-only version: cards leave on E.in over 22 f, with travel scaled by (1 + 0.1 * index).
- **Use when:** A crescendo near the end that proves breadth (many apps, templates, outputs) and clears the stage for the lockup or a hero stat; the film's single biggest motion spike.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or minimal films, more than once per film, or when the cards' content has to be read (nothing in the swarm is legible). If it reveals the lockup, the lockup still holds only 1.5-2.0 s.
